name: An interpreter too old for the kit is told so before anything is imported
summary: Every program of the kit that needs Python 3.10 checks the interpreter before any other import: started with an older one it writes one line to stderr and exits 2, naming the program, the version needed, the version and path of the interpreter found, that nothing was carried out, and what to do. They are endpoint.py, client.py, admin.py, office_service.py, http_service.py, http_client.py, lifecycle.py, coordination.py, capabilities.py, requirement_records.py, setup_assistant.py, worker.py, worker_gate.py and tools/office_verify.py; a test lists every file with a __main__ block and fails for one that has neither the check nor a place on the short lists of programs that run or start under 3.6 (ssh_forced_command.py and tools/office_release.py on purpose). The check is the first statement after the docstring and `import sys`, written out in each file, and the files stay readable by Python 3.6. client.py shows the endpoint's line without "outcome may be uncertain", and with a forced command says that the authorized_keys line must be printed again. Over SSH the "python" key of the client configuration names the interpreter on the server.
